name: Run the customer research sweep
trigger: scheduled monthly | on demand before an avatar or positioning refresh
human_role: what a customer insights analyst does at the start of every research cycle
inputs_required: brand brain: product list and SKUs
connector: reviews export (site + marketplace)
connector: support desk export (tickets, returns, calls)
connector: GA4 / on-site search log
budget ledger: remaining balance for any paid deep-research pass

steps.name: Pull and tag reviews by star band
steps.does: Export every review per SKU with rating and date. Read 1-2 star for the real objection under the surface complaint. Read 4-5 star for the job the product actually did. Flag Hinglish and regional-language phrasing as-is, do not translate away the voice.
steps.output: tagged quote set by star band, objection frequency list
steps.check: every quote has SKU, star, source and date; reviewer full name stripped

steps.name: Pull and tag support signal
steps.does: Export tickets, return reasons and call transcripts for the period. Tag by the underlying failure, not the customer's stated request. Flag sizing, fit or delivery-delay anxieties (failed-delivery and address-validation complaints; India-relevant: COD refusal reasons, markets: IN, reads null for US).
steps.output: struggle theme list, quote set with consent flag
steps.check: consent status logged before any quote leaves the ticket system

steps.name: Run forum and social listening
steps.does: Search Reddit, Quora, Instagram comments and relevant social threads in the avatar's own words for language, objections and sub-avatars a review file misses. Include WhatsApp-forwarded review threads where the brand's customers use that channel (markets: IN, EU, LATAM).
steps.output: language bank additions, sub-avatar candidate notes
steps.check: every source has a URL and date; nothing from a private group is quoted

steps.name: Mine on-site search and browse-without-buy
steps.does: Read the brand's own on-site search terms and sessions that browsed a category or PDP without adding to cart, for what shoppers were actually trying to find.
steps.check: terms are deduplicated and volume-ranked before being called a pattern

steps.name: Cross-check patterns across sources
steps.does: Line up review, ticket, social and search findings. Keep only patterns that show up in 2 or more independent sources. Drop single contradictory outliers.
steps.check: every pattern kept lists which 2+ sources it came from

steps.name: Verify one prioritized claim with AI deep research, if needed
steps.does: If a pattern is high-stakes (would change the primary avatar or a positioning claim) and thin on quotes, run one AI deep-research pass on that single candidate and verify every returned quote at its original source before it is used.
steps.check: budget.py checked before the call; every quote traced back to its live source page
steps.ask_founder_if: the verification would push the run over the working stop ($160)

steps.name: Update the verbatim language bank
steps.does: Append new exact-quoted phrases to the per-avatar language bank, tagged by source and repetition count, anonymized.
steps.check: no full name or contact detail is stored with a quote

steps.name: Hand off findings for avatar work
steps.does: Package the cross-verified patterns, quote sets and language bank update as the input packet for the avatar-record or positioning workflow that runs next.
steps.output: research packet, logged in the registry
steps.check: packet lists every source type used and what was not available

outputs: tagged quote set by star band
qa: every quote has a source and date
no full name kept
a pattern is only real with 2+ independent sources
nothing from a private support conversation left without a consent flag
read_point: not a metric read. Freshness re-checked at the next monthly cycle; a pattern older than one quarter is re-verified before reuse.
typical_duration: agent time 2-4 hours across sources; add 1-2 days wait if a support desk or GA4 export has to be requested.
subagents: Avatar Research Miner runs steps 1-4 so bulk raw text never enters the main agent's context

name: Design and run a customer interview program
trigger: on demand | event: a research packet has a gap no passive source can fill
human_role: what a founder or researcher does to hear the job in the customer's own words
inputs_required: research packet from BRAND-W01
customer list or panel access
founder availability for the incentive decision

steps.name: Name the open question
steps.does: State exactly what the interview must learn that reviews, tickets and social could not (a trigger moment, a fired alternative, a hidden social dimension).
steps.check: the question cannot already be answered from BRAND-W01 output

steps.name: Write the interview guide
steps.does: Draft 8-12 open questions in job-to-be-done order: the trigger, the struggle, the alternatives tried, the moment of choosing, the after-state. No leading or feature-fishing questions.
steps.check: no question can be answered yes/no; no question names the brand's own feature first

steps.name: Pick channel and incentive
steps.does: Recommend a channel (call, video, SMS or voice note thread; WhatsApp voice note thread where the brand's customers use it, markets: IN, EU, LATAM) and a proportionate incentive (a discount code or small gift, not cash that could bias answers) sized to the brand's own economics.
steps.check: incentive cost is computed against contribution margin, not guessed
steps.ask_founder_if: the incentive plan needs a founder-approved budget line

steps.name: Recruit the sample
steps.does: Pull 8-12 candidates across at least 2 purchase recency bands (recent buyer, lapsed buyer) from the customer list.
steps.check: no single cohort is more than 70% of the sample

steps.name: Hand off or run the conversations
steps.does: If the founder or team runs the calls, hand off the guide and a note-taking template. If a person the agent can't be, stop here and mark this a human_assist step.
steps.check: every scheduled interview has a guide attached
steps.ask_founder_if: no one is available to run the conversations this cycle

steps.name: Log transcripts
steps.does: File each transcript or note set with date, respondent recency band, and consent status.
steps.check: every transcript has a consent flag before any quote is reused

steps.name: Extract patterns
steps.does: Pull job statement material, forces (push, pull, anxiety, habit) and fired alternatives from the transcripts. Cross-check against BRAND-W01 patterns.
steps.check: every finding cites which transcript it came from

steps.name: Route to avatar work
steps.does: Hand the findings packet to BRAND-W05 (avatar record) with a note on what changed from the passive-data picture.
steps.check: the note names any avatar assumption the interviews overturned

qa: every question is open, not leading
every transcript has a consent flag
incentive cost computed, not guessed
read_point: not a metric read; a qualitative evidence build feeding the next avatar cycle.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours to prepare and synthesize; 1-3 weeks wait for scheduling and running 8-12 conversations.

name: Design and field a customer survey
trigger: quarterly | on demand to confirm a research finding at scale
human_role: what a researcher does to check a finding against the wider customer base, never to discover a new job
inputs_required: a specific finding from BRAND-W01 or BRAND-W02 to confirm
connector: email/SMS platform (draft only)
customer list segmented by recency or tier

steps.name: State the confirm-or-deny question
steps.does: Write the one claim the survey exists to test (for example, 'gifting is the #1 purchase occasion for tier 2 buyers'). Reject any survey brief that instead asks 'what do you want.'
steps.check: the hypothesis already has qualitative evidence behind it from W01/W02

steps.name: Pick the survey type
steps.does: Choose identity, post-purchase, or NPS/relationship format to match the question. Keep it under 6 questions.
steps.check: 6 questions or fewer; no double-barreled question

steps.name: Draft the send, do not send it
steps.does: Draft the survey invite in the email/SMS platform (connector is read + draft only, no send permission).
steps.check: draft only; no send action taken
steps.ask_founder_if: always, before send: this connector cannot send without approval

steps.name: Founder approves and sends
steps.does: Founder reviews the draft and either sends it themselves or approves the send.
steps.check: send is logged as founder-approved, not agent-executed

steps.name: Collect and clean responses
steps.does: Pull responses once the window closes. Drop straight-line and under-10-second responses.
steps.check: junk-response rate reported, not hidden

steps.name: Score against the hypothesis
steps.does: Compute the confirm/deny rate in code against the original hypothesis line.
steps.check: result reported with n, never as a vague 'most customers'

steps.name: Route the result
steps.does: File the result to the brand brain and the workflow that raised the original finding.
steps.check: result changes or confirms a specific record, named explicitly

qa: 6 questions or fewer
survey confirms an existing finding, never fishes for a new one
send only after founder approval
read_point: scored the day the response window closes, with sample size reported.
typical_duration: agent time 2-3 hours to design and score; 1-2 weeks wait for the response window.

name: Research competitors and public benchmarks
trigger: scheduled monthly | on demand before a positioning or naming cycle
human_role: what a competitive-intelligence analyst does before any positioning claim is written
inputs_required: named competitor set (direct and adjacent)
brand brain: category and price tier
budget ledger

steps.name: Confirm the competitive set
steps.does: List direct rivals plus real alternatives a shopper would compare against, including doing nothing and the generic marketplace listing (Amazon, Walmart Marketplace or Target Plus equivalents; Flipkart or Meesho for an India-market comparison, markets: IN).
steps.check: list includes at least one non-obvious adjacent alternative

steps.name: Pull public ad signal
steps.does: Search the Meta Ad Library for each competitor's live ads: formats, hooks, offer structure. Public library only, never the brand's own ad account data.
steps.output: competitor ad signal notes with dates
steps.check: every note is labeled 'signal, not proof' per the competitor-material rule

steps.name: Pull public page, review and Q&A signal
steps.does: Read each competitor's PDP, About page, and public reviews/Q&A for claims made, price anchors, and unmet complaints.
steps.check: every claim quoted carries a URL and date

steps.name: Check budget before any paid lookup
steps.does: If any step needs a paid API or tool call, check the ledger first.
steps.check: no paid call proceeds without a logged check
steps.ask_founder_if: the pull would exceed the working stop

steps.name: Map the mainstream avatar per competitor
steps.does: Infer who each competitor is obviously talking to, from their imagery, copy and price point.
steps.check: inference is labeled inference, not fact

steps.name: Check market health signals
steps.does: Note category growth or decline signals: new entrants, price compression, review-volume trend.
steps.check: every signal dated within the last 12 months or flagged stale

steps.name: File the competitor packet
steps.does: Package ad signal, page signal, avatar reads and market health into one dated packet for positioning and naming work.
steps.check: packet carries no competitor text, logo, product photo or face copied in

qa: every source has a URL and date
nothing copied, only described
labeled signal not proof throughout
read_point: refreshed monthly; a packet older than 60 days is re-pulled before it feeds a positioning statement.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours for a 5-8 competitor set.
subagents: Avatar Research Miner can run steps 2-3 at scale across a large competitive set

name: Build and gate a new avatar record
trigger: event: a new avatar is needed, or the quarterly recheck finds the current one stale
human_role: what a brand strategist does to turn scattered research into one usable customer record
inputs_required: research packet from BRAND-W01 (and W02/W03 if run)
competitor packet from BRAND-W04 if positioning-relevant
founder sign-off on which candidate to build

steps.name: Draft the job-to-be-done statement
steps.does: Write the job in a situation: 'when [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome].' Cover functional, emotional and social sides.
steps.check: passes the verb-noun test and the cross-category test (the job exists outside this exact product too)

steps.name: Name the 4 forces
steps.does: Identify the push (problem), pull (attraction to a solution), anxiety (what could go wrong), and habit (inertia keeping them with the status quo).
steps.check: each force has at least one verbatim quote

steps.name: Name the fired alternative
steps.does: State what the customer was doing, or considering, before this product (a competitor, a DIY fix, or doing nothing).
steps.check: traces to a specific quote or competitor data point, not assumed

steps.name: Build the objection map
steps.does: Pair every named objection with the real thing that removed it for a real customer (a review, a support reply, a product change). Where relevant, turn a pattern into a fit or size-confidence angle and a support macro draft.
steps.check: every objection has 2+ quoted sources; every remover is something that actually happened, not a hoped-for fix

steps.name: Build the 5W profile and trigger moment
steps.does: Who, what, when, where, why, plus the specific moment that starts the buying process (a wedding date set, a monsoon starting, a festival approaching).
steps.check: trigger moment is a specific event, not a vague season

steps.name: Assemble the full record
steps.does: Pull job, forces, fired alternative, objection map, 5W, trigger and quote set into one avatar record.
steps.check: every required field is present or explicitly marked missing

steps.name: Set the status flag
steps.does: Mark the record 'confirmed' only if built from 2+ independent source types with at least one first-party source (for an existing brand). Otherwise mark 'provisional.'
steps.check: status flag matches the actual source count, not optimism

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the record with its sources for founder approval before it becomes the record other specialists cite.
steps.check: card shows sources and the provisional/confirmed flag plainly
steps.ask_founder_if: always: this is a founder_gate capability

steps.name: Write to the registry and brand brain
steps.does: Log the decision and, if approved, write the avatar record into the brand brain customer section.
steps.check: a rejected record is logged with the founder's reason, not silently dropped

qa: every field traces to a quote or is marked missing
status flag matches real source count
founder decision logged either way
read_point: revisited every quarter (BRAND-W07) or when a brief citing it stops converting.
typical_duration: agent time 4-6 hours once research is in hand; founder review adds 1-3 days.
subagents: Avatar Research Miner can pre-cluster the quote sets before this workflow starts

name: Discover, rank and prioritize avatar candidates
trigger: scheduled quarterly
human_role: what a strategist does before picking which customer to build the next cycle's work around
inputs_required: all avatar candidates surfaced this quarter (from W01, W02, W04, W08)
current primary avatar record
metric contract: revenue and repeat-rate by known segment where trackable

steps.name: List every candidate
steps.does: Pull every avatar candidate surfaced across this quarter's research, including sub-avatars flagged in social listening.
steps.check: every candidate names which run surfaced it

steps.name: Require a cross-source pattern
steps.does: Drop any candidate that appears in only one source type.
steps.check: remaining candidates each cite 2+ source types

steps.name: Score reach and fit
steps.does: Estimate each candidate's addressable size against the brand's own customer and traffic data, and its fit to current product and margin.
steps.check: scores computed in code from real fields, not estimated in prose

steps.name: Rank and pick the primary
steps.does: Rank by reach x fit x evidence strength. Recommend a primary avatar for the cycle and note runner-ups.
steps.check: the current primary is not kept by default without being re-scored

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the ranked list and recommendation for the founder to confirm, override, or ask for another cycle of evidence.
steps.check: card shows why each runner-up ranked below the pick

steps.name: Route the pick
steps.does: If the primary changed, trigger BRAND-W05 to build or refresh that avatar's full record.
steps.check: a changed primary always triggers a fresh record build, never reuses an old provisional one

qa: every candidate has 2+ source types
scores computed in code
decision logged either way
read_point: quarterly, alongside the general avatar audit (BRAND-W07).
typical_duration: agent time 2-3 hours; founder review 1-3 days.

name: Segment and maintain avatars on a cadence
trigger: quarterly | event: new price tier, channel or subscription line
human_role: what a strategist does to keep the customer record honest and correctly split over time
inputs_required: current avatar record(s)
brand brain: pricing tiers, channels, B2B or subscription lines
briefs written since the last audit, to check citation

steps.name: Check for a split trigger
steps.does: Check whether a new price tier, buyer-versus-user split (for example, a gifting buyer versus the person who wears the piece), B2B line, or subscription churn pattern has changed the underlying job.
steps.check: a split is only proposed when the job itself differs, not just the SKU

steps.name: Split the record if warranted
steps.does: Create a separate avatar record for the new segment, reusing shared quotes but writing a distinct job statement and objection map where they differ.
steps.check: each split record stands on its own evidence, not copy-pasted from the parent

steps.name: Audit citation
steps.does: Check which briefs and pages have cited the current avatar record since the last audit, and whether product still earns the win described in it.
steps.check: note names any brief that cited a stale or wrong field

steps.name: Re-check the dominant avatar
steps.does: Re-run the source-count and freshness check on the primary avatar; flag if evidence is older than 2 quarters.
steps.check: verdict is date-stamped, not assumed current

steps.name: Refresh what's stale
steps.does: If evidence is stale, route back to BRAND-W01 for a fresh research pass before editing the record.
steps.check: never edits a record from memory without new evidence

steps.name: Founder gate on any material change
steps.does: Any split, merge or material rewrite of a live avatar record goes to the founder before it replaces what specialists are citing.
steps.check: a live record is never silently overwritten

steps.name: Log and publish
steps.does: Write the approved version to the brand brain and note the audit date for the next cycle.
steps.check: prior version is kept in history, not deleted

qa: a split needs a real job difference, not just a SKU difference
no record edited without new evidence
material change always founder-gated
read_point: quarterly, or immediately on a triggering event (new tier, channel, subscription line).
typical_duration: agent time 2-4 hours; founder review 1-3 days if a change is proposed.

name: Run the untapped avatar discovery pipeline
trigger: on demand, when the category is saturated and the product has no real point of difference left to claim
human_role: what a strategist does to find a customer competitors have not claimed, instead of fighting for the same one
inputs_required: competitor packet (BRAND-W04) covering who every rival obviously targets
current avatar record
brand brain: product capabilities

steps.name: Map who is already claimed
steps.does: List the avatar every visible competitor is obviously serving, from BRAND-W04's per-competitor avatar reads.
steps.check: map covers every competitor in the set, not just the top 2

steps.name: List adjacent jobs the product could also do
steps.does: From the product's real capabilities, list jobs it could serve beyond the claimed avatar's job (a gifting job, a professional-use job, a different life stage).
steps.check: every candidate job is something the product can actually do today, not a roadmap wish

steps.name: Search for evidence the adjacent job is real
steps.does: Search reviews, forums and search terms (own and public) for signs someone already uses or wants the product for that adjacent job.
steps.check: a candidate with zero found evidence is dropped, not carried forward on hope

steps.name: Size the candidate
steps.does: Run a lightweight market-sizing pass on the strongest 1-2 candidates.
steps.check: sizing uses the brand's own AOV and margin, not an assumed one

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the untapped-avatar candidates with evidence and sizing for a founder decision on whether to pursue.
steps.check: recommendation names the evidence and the size, not just the idea

steps.name: Route to avatar build
steps.does: If approved, hand off to BRAND-W05 to build the full avatar record for the new candidate.
steps.check: a rejected candidate is logged with the reason so it is not re-proposed unchanged

qa: every candidate checked against real evidence
sizing done in code from the brand's own numbers
read_point: not a metric read; re-run whenever the category feels saturated again.
typical_duration: agent time 4-6 hours.

name: Map the category ladder and the XY positioning map
trigger: event: a new positioning cycle starts, or the competitive set materially changes
human_role: what a strategist does before any positioning claim gets written
inputs_required: competitor packet (BRAND-W04)
brand brain: category, price tier, product facts

steps.name: List every rung of the category ladder
steps.does: List the category itself, the sub-category, every real product alternative, and doing nothing, as rungs a shopper could pick instead of this brand.
steps.check: ladder includes 'doing nothing' as a rung

steps.name: List the real competitive set
steps.does: List every brand or option a shopper would actually compare against, not only the obvious direct rivals.
steps.check: list includes at least one indirect or adjacent-category alternative

steps.name: Choose the two axes
steps.does: Pick two axes that matter to the avatar's actual decision (for example, price versus trust-signal, or craft versus convenience), not two axes that flatter this brand.
steps.check: axes are drawn from what the avatar record says they weigh, not picked to make an empty corner appear

steps.name: Plot every alternative
steps.does: Plot the brand and every real alternative from the competitive set on the two axes, using facts from the competitor packet.
steps.check: every plotted point cites the fact that placed it there

steps.name: Identify open corners
steps.does: Mark which corners of the map have no occupant, and whether that emptiness means opportunity or means no one wants that combination.
steps.check: an empty corner is checked against demand evidence before being called an opportunity

steps.name: File for positioning work
steps.does: Hand the ladder and map to BRAND-W10 for the positioning statement.
steps.check: nothing is claimed as positioning yet; this step only maps the field

qa: every plotted point cites a fact
axes reflect what the avatar actually weighs
doing nothing is on the ladder
read_point: refreshed whenever the competitive set changes materially, at minimum once a year.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours.

name: Draft, audit and test the positioning statement
trigger: event: new or refreshed positioning, following BRAND-W09
human_role: what a strategist does to turn a mapped field into one line a shopper reads and believes
inputs_required: category ladder and XY map (BRAND-W09)
avatar record
voice sheet if one exists
claims tiers (approved / site-backed / forbidden)

steps.name: Answer the 6 positioning questions in writing
steps.does: Write out: for whom, for what category, against what alternative, what benefit, why believe it, why now. No skipping to the tagline first.
steps.check: every answer traces to the avatar record or a verified fact, not an assertion

steps.name: Draft the 3-sentence promise
steps.does: Write the promise in 3 sentences: the change, the mechanism, the proof.
steps.check: every claim in it passes shared/claim-check against the claims tiers

steps.name: Cut to the one line
steps.does: Cut the promise to the single line a scrolling shopper would actually read and remember.
steps.check: line passes the strip test: it fails if a competitor's name could replace this brand's and it would still read true

steps.name: Run the positioning checklist
steps.does: Check the statement against the fixed checklist (clear, ownable, provable, durable, not a disputed stat).
steps.check: a fail on any item blocks moving forward until fixed

steps.name: If no open slot exists, search for a creneau or reframe
steps.does: When the XY map shows every corner already occupied, search for an unclaimed dimension, take the deliberate against-position, or reframe the category around a shared frustration the avatar already voices.
steps.check: the reframe is grounded in a frustration the avatar record already documents, not invented

steps.name: Test 2 frames against each other
steps.does: Where two credible framings exist, design a small test (message test in an ad, a landing headline split, or an AI-persona pretest) to see which the avatar responds to before committing.
steps.output: test design and, once run, a result
steps.check: test has a stated read point before it starts

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the statement, promise, checklist result and any test result to the founder.
steps.check: card shows the checklist result plainly, pass or fail

steps.name: Publish
steps.does: Write the approved positioning statement to the brand brain identity section.
steps.check: old positioning is versioned, not deleted

qa: every claim passes claim-check
strip test passed
checklist failures blocked from shipping
read_point: revisited whenever the competitive set or avatar changes materially.
typical_duration: agent time 4-6 hours; founder review 1-3 days; a message test adds 1-2 weeks if run.

name: Size the market and audit pricing position
trigger: event: new niche or product idea | quarterly pricing audit
human_role: what an operator does before believing a niche is worth building, and before a price drifts out of position
inputs_required: metric contract: AOV, gross margin, contribution margin, repeat_rate_90d/365d
candidate niche or product idea, if sizing one
competitor packet: category price range

steps.name: Compute repeat buyers needed to sustain the business
steps.does: From this store's own AOV and margin, compute how many repeat buyers at what frequency would sustain the business or the candidate line.
steps.check: computed in code from real fields; missing fields show as unavailable, not assumed

steps.name: Check parent market and sub-niche size
steps.does: Look for an independent size signal for the category and the specific niche (search volume, subreddit size, marketplace listing count, review-count proxy).
steps.check: signal has a URL and date; a niche with no findable signal is flagged 'unproven,' not sized anyway

steps.name: Place on the price-by-customer-count matrix
steps.does: Place the candidate on a matrix of price point against needed customer count, to see if it is a volume play or a margin play.
steps.check: placement stated as a range, not a false-precise single number

steps.name: Check current price against the category's learned range
steps.does: Compare the brand's live price to the category range found in the competitor packet.
steps.check: verdict states which competitors set the range boundaries

steps.name: Audit premium signals
steps.does: Check whether packaging, page copy, and current discount cadence still support a premium story, if one is claimed.
steps.check: a high discount_rate next to a premium claim is flagged explicitly, not smoothed over

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present sizing and pricing findings together; both are founder_gate decisions.
steps.check: card separates the sizing question from the pricing question clearly

steps.name: Log the result
steps.does: Write the decision and figures to the registry.
steps.check: figures kept alongside the decision for the next quarter's comparison

qa: all arithmetic in code
missing inputs marked unavailable, never assumed
a sizing claim always cites its independent signal
read_point: market sizing at idea time; pricing audit every quarter.
typical_duration: agent time 2-3 hours.

name: Run a naming project, brand or product
trigger: on demand | event: new SKU or collection needs a name
human_role: what a naming consultant does from a blank page to a cleared, presentable name
inputs_required: brand brain: category, product facts, target avatar
target markets and languages for clearance
scope: full brand name or a lighter product/SKU/collection name

steps.name: Set the scope
steps.does: Decide whether this is a full brand-naming project or a lighter product, SKU or collection name screen. Default to a descriptive, benefit-first title for search where a brand name is not needed.
steps.check: scope decision stated before generation starts, so effort matches the stakes

steps.name: Run the category, product and buyer audit
steps.does: Review the category's naming conventions, the product's real attributes, and the avatar's language, so generated names are grounded, not generic.
steps.check: brief lists what the name must NOT do (no forbidden claim, no confusable-with-competitor sound)

steps.name: Generate far more candidates than feels necessary
steps.does: Generate candidates across all naming types (descriptive, suggestive, invented, founder, evocative) using AI for volume, human judgment applied at review, not at generation.
steps.check: list spans multiple naming types, not one flavor repeated

steps.name: Screen on the 7 core qualities
steps.does: Score every candidate: distinctive, meaningful, memorable, brief, positive, extendable, protectable. Test sound and syllable count out loud. Avoid acronym and generic-name traps.
steps.check: each finalist has all 7 scores shown, not a single overall number

steps.name: Clear finalists for trademark, domain and language risk
steps.does: Search the USPTO trademark database and international equivalents, check name + industry-term collisions, check domain and social handle availability, and check meaning and sound in relevant languages (Spanish for US customers, plus Hindi or any other export-market language when the brand sells into that market).
steps.check: every finalist has a status: clear, risk, or needs-legal
steps.ask_founder_if: a finalist needs a paid legal opinion or filing

steps.name: Mock up the finalists
steps.does: Present the top 2-3 cleared names in realistic mock-ups (packaging, PDP title, a spoken-aloud test) rather than as a bare word list.
steps.check: mock-ups use the real product photo, not an invented render, where accuracy matters

steps.name: Write the short story and tagline (full brand names only)
steps.does: For a full brand-naming project, write nomenclature notes, a short brand story, and a tagline that passes the strip test.
steps.check: tagline fails the strip test if a competitor's name could swap in and it would still read true

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the finalized name package for founder decision.
inputs: naming deliverable or scored SKU shortlist
steps.check: card shows clearance status plainly next to the name

steps.name: Publish
steps.does: Log the decision; if approved, write the name into the brand brain or product catalogue as applicable.
steps.output: registry entry, brand brain or catalogue update
steps.check: a rejected name is logged with the reason, not silently reused later

qa: candidates span multiple naming types
every finalist has a real clearance status
tagline passes the strip test
read_point: not a metric read; naming is a one-time deliverable per project.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 days for a full brand name; 1-2 hours for a SKU/collection name; legal clearance can add 1-2 weeks if a paid opinion is needed.

name: Decide brand architecture for a new line or market
trigger: event: a new product line, category extension or market entry is proposed
human_role: what a brand architect decides before a new line ships under a name
inputs_required: proposed new line or market
current brand equity and guidelines
avatar overlap between current brand and the new line's likely buyer

steps.name: Run the teeter-totter test
steps.does: Check whether the new line would pull equity away from the parent brand's core meaning if given the master brand name (does adding this make the master brand mean less, not more).
steps.check: verdict is written as a specific mechanism, not a feeling

steps.name: Run the shopping-list test
steps.does: Check whether a shopper would naturally put the new line on the same mental shopping list as the current brand, or whether it reads as a different errand entirely.
steps.check: verdict names the specific shopper behavior it is based on

steps.name: Check avatar overlap
steps.does: Compare the new line's likely buyer against the current primary avatar for real overlap, not assumed overlap.
steps.check: overlap stated as high, partial or low, with the evidence

steps.name: Default to one master brand for a small brand
steps.does: Unless a real reason surfaces in steps 1-3 (equity dilution risk, no shopping-list overlap, real reputational separation needed), recommend the master-brand name over a new name, since a small brand cannot afford to build two names.
steps.output: architecture recommendation (master brand vs new name)
steps.check: a 'new name' recommendation must name the specific reason the default was overridden

steps.name: Route naming if a new name is warranted
steps.does: If a new name is recommended, hand off to BRAND-W12 for the naming project.
steps.check: routing happens only after the architecture decision, never before it

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the recommendation and reasoning to the founder.
steps.check: card states the default and why it was or was not overridden

steps.name: Log the decision
steps.does: Write the decision and reasoning to the registry and brand brain.
steps.check: reasoning is kept, not just the yes/no outcome

qa: default to one master brand unless a named reason overrides it
every verdict is a specific mechanism, not a feeling
read_point: not a metric read; a one-time architecture decision per new line or market.
typical_duration: agent time 2-3 hours; founder review 1-3 days.

name: Draft the brand story, voice sheet and promise
trigger: on demand | event: new brand, voice drift found, or a new promise/tagline is needed
human_role: what a brand writer does to give every future writer and model a stable voice to sound like
inputs_required: founder's vision and values, in their own words
real customer understanding (avatar record)
Kevin's liked and disliked copy examples

steps.name: Draft the founder or brand story
steps.does: Write the story in a self, us, now structure: who the founder is, what the shared struggle with the customer is, why this matters right now. Keep it stable for years, not campaign-specific.
steps.check: story contains no invented biographical fact; founder confirms every detail

steps.name: Set a default voice if none exists
steps.does: If no voice sheet exists yet, set a plain, direct default voice (short sentences, no jargon, digits not words) so copy work is not blocked while the real sheet is built.
steps.check: clearly marked 'default, not final'

steps.name: Collect liked and disliked examples
steps.does: Gather Kevin's liked and disliked copy examples from past work, real or reference.
steps.check: every example is real, sourced copy, not invented for the exercise

steps.name: Derive 4-8 voice traits
steps.does: From the examples, derive 4-8 traits, each with a liked example, a disliked example, and a one-line rule.
steps.output: voice and tone sheet (short + full versions)
steps.check: every trait has both a real liked and a real disliked example

steps.name: Draft the 3-sentence promise and tagline candidates
steps.does: Write the promise (change, mechanism, proof) and 3-5 tagline candidates.
steps.check: every claim in the promise passes shared/claim-check

steps.name: Run the strip test
steps.does: Cut candidates that would still read true with a competitor's name swapped in.
steps.check: at least one candidate is ownable and specific to this brand

steps.name: Design a recall test, if a signature line is being chosen
steps.does: For a candidate meant to become a signature line, design a small recall-based test (does the shopper remember it after seeing an ad or page once).
steps.output: test design and, once run, a recall result
steps.check: test has a stated read point before it runs

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present story, voice sheet and promise/tagline together for founder approval.
steps.check: card separates the three deliverables so each can be approved or sent back independently

steps.name: Publish
steps.does: Write approved pieces to the brand brain identity section.
steps.check: a default voice is replaced, not left stacked alongside the real one

qa: every voice trait has real liked/disliked examples
every promise claim passes claim-check
tagline passes the strip test
read_point: voice sheet re-checked whenever drift is found in the consistency audit (BRAND-W17).
typical_duration: agent time 4-8 hours; founder review 2-4 days.

name: Build a messaging hierarchy for a page or channel
trigger: event: new campaign, page, or channel needs a message stack
human_role: what a messaging strategist writes so every asset on a page or channel leads with the same one idea
inputs_required: positioning statement
avatar record and objection map
the specific page or channel type (homepage, PDP, email, ads)

steps.name: Name the one big idea
steps.does: State the single idea this page or channel must lead with, drawn from the positioning statement, not invented fresh.
steps.check: big idea traces directly to the approved positioning statement

steps.name: Rank up to 3 supporting messages
steps.does: Pull the strongest supporting messages from the objection map and avatar record, ranked by how much friction each removes.
steps.check: each supporting message maps to a specific objection or force

steps.name: Fit the stack to the page type
steps.does: Adjust order and depth for the page or channel: homepage leads broad, PDP leads with the objection most likely at that SKU's price point, email leads with the relationship stage, ads lead with the hook.
steps.check: stack respects the writing rules: short sentences, digits, no em dashes

steps.name: Claim-check the stack
steps.does: Run every message through claim-check against the claims tiers.
steps.check: no message ships with an untraced or forbidden claim

steps.name: Hand off to the executing specialist
steps.does: Route the finished hierarchy to the Site specialist (page) or Paid Creative/Copy specialist (ad, email) to execute; this agent never writes the final page or ad itself.
steps.check: packet is a message stack, not a finished draft, respecting the ownership boundary

steps.name: Log the hierarchy
steps.does: File the approved hierarchy to the registry so future briefs for this page/channel reuse it instead of drifting.
steps.check: hierarchy is retrievable by page/channel type for reuse

qa: big idea traces to positioning
every message passes claim-check
stack respects the writing rules
read_point: not a metric read; re-run when positioning or the avatar changes, or a page underperforms.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 hours per page/channel.

name: Brief visual identity and assemble the brand guidelines document
trigger: event: new brand or a major identity refresh
human_role: what a brand designer's creative director briefs before a designer ever opens a file
inputs_required: positioning statement
voice and tone sheet
avatar record (aesthetic preferences, price-tier expectations)

steps.name: Write the mood and reference direction
steps.does: Describe the intended mood, palette, typography and photography direction in words and referenced mood only. This agent never generates the final visual assets.
steps.check: brief is words and mood references, no invented final logo or asset

steps.name: Hand the reference pull to the Reference Scout
steps.does: Route the mood brief to the Reference Scout for real, mood-only visual references, never competitor logos or product photos to copy.
steps.check: references are for layout and mood only, never copied

steps.name: Draft logo and mark rules
steps.does: Write the rules for logo clear space, minimum size, and misuse examples, once a mark exists.
steps.check: rules include at least 3 concrete misuse examples

steps.name: Assemble visual language section
steps.does: Package palette, typography and photography direction into the visual language section.
steps.check: every color and font choice ties back to the mood brief's reasoning

steps.name: Assemble language rules section
steps.does: Fold in the voice and tone sheet as the language rules section.
steps.check: section is the actual voice sheet, not a rewritten summary of it

steps.name: Build the expressions section
steps.does: Show 3-5 applied examples (a PDP header, an email, an ad) demonstrating the rules together.
steps.check: every applied example passes claim-check and the writing rules

steps.name: Run the completeness checklist
steps.does: Check the 4 parts (mark rules, visual language, language rules, expressions) are all present before calling the document done.
steps.check: a missing part blocks publishing, it does not ship as 'to be added later'

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the assembled guidelines document for founder approval.
steps.check: card shows the checklist result plainly

steps.name: Publish
steps.does: Write the approved guidelines to the brand brain and file the document.
steps.check: prior guidelines version is kept in history

qa: mood only, nothing copied
all 4 parts present before publishing
every applied example passes claim-check
read_point: revisited at a major refresh; drift is caught monthly by BRAND-W17 in between.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 days; Reference Scout turnaround adds hours; founder review 2-5 days.
subagents: Reference Scout pulls mood-only visual references

name: Audit brand consistency and diagnose the perception gap
trigger: scheduled monthly (consistency) | quarterly, run together with the perception-gap pass
human_role: what a brand manager does walking the live brand against its own rulebook, then checking the rulebook against reality
inputs_required: brand guidelines document
voice and tone sheet
live site, ad and email surfaces
recent reviews, social mentions and survey results

steps.name: Walk the site against guidelines
steps.does: Crawl key site pages (home, PDP, checkout) and check against logo rules, visual language and voice.
steps.check: every drift item cites the specific rule it breaks

steps.name: Walk live ads and email against guidelines
steps.does: Check current live ad creative and recent email/SMS sends against the same rules.
steps.check: read-only check; no ad account write attempted

steps.name: Score drift severity
steps.does: Rank each drift item by how visible and how far from the rule it is.
steps.check: ranking is computed from visibility and distance, not gut feel

steps.name: Compare stated identity to what customers actually say
steps.does: Compare the positioning statement, voice sheet and claims against what reviews, social mentions and survey results actually say about the brand.
steps.check: gap note quotes real customer language, not a paraphrase

steps.name: Name the gap type
steps.does: Classify each gap as the brand under-claiming (customers already believe more than the brand says) or over-claiming (customers do not believe what the brand says).
steps.check: an over-claim gap is flagged as higher priority than an under-claim

steps.name: Draft fixes
steps.does: For each drift or gap item, draft a specific fix (a page change, an ad note, a wording change) sized to what can actually be done.
steps.check: every fix names the owning specialist (Site, Media, Creative) for execution

steps.name: Founder gate on any identity-level fix
steps.does: A fix that changes the voice sheet, positioning or guidelines themselves needs founder approval; a fix that is just correcting a live asset to match existing rules does not.
steps.check: only identity-level fixes are gated; routine corrections are not held up
steps.ask_founder_if: a fix would change the guidelines or positioning themselves

steps.name: Route and log
steps.does: Send routine fixes directly to the owning specialist; log identity-level fixes to the registry with the founder's decision.
steps.check: every fix is tracked to a closing status next month, not dropped

qa: every drift cites the specific rule broken
gap note quotes real customer language
over-claim gaps prioritized over under-claim
read_point: monthly for drift; quarterly for the perception-gap comparison.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours.

name: Track brand health signals
trigger: scheduled monthly
human_role: what a brand manager tracks separately from any single campaign's performance
inputs_required: connector: Google Search Console (branded search volume)
review rating and count over time
social mention data, where collectable

steps.name: Pull branded search volume
steps.does: Pull branded search query volume and trend from Search Console.
steps.check: trend covers a rolling 12 months where available; missing months marked unavailable

steps.name: Pull review rating and count trend
steps.does: Track review_rating and review_count over time from the metric contract.
steps.check: computed in code from the contract, not estimated

steps.name: Pull mention and sentiment signal, where available
steps.does: Check for any collectable public mention or sentiment data; if no source exists yet, mark this field unavailable rather than guessing a sentiment score.
inputs: public web, if a source exists
steps.check: never fabricates a sentiment score with no real source behind it

steps.name: Track repeat behavior trend
steps.does: Pull repeat_rate_90d and repeat_rate_365d trend from the metric contract as a brand-strength proxy, separate from any one campaign.
steps.check: kept separate from campaign-level ROAS reporting

steps.name: Assemble the brand health line
steps.does: Combine branded search, review trend, mention signal and repeat trend into one dated brand health line.
steps.check: each series shows its own freshness date, not one blended 'as of' date

steps.name: Flag material moves
steps.does: Flag any series that moved more than a set threshold since last month for founder attention.
steps.check: threshold is stated, not a subjective 'looks different'

steps.name: File the report
steps.does: Log the report to the registry and the monthly review.
steps.check: report is retrievable month over month for trend comparison

qa: missing data marked unavailable, never zero
every series dated
no fabricated sentiment score
read_point: monthly, trend read over a rolling 12 months where data exists.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 hours.

name: Design community and loyalty cohorts for advocacy
trigger: on demand
human_role: what a community lead designs before inviting anyone into an exclusive group
inputs_required: avatar record
current top advocates (from reviews, repeat purchase, social mentions)
brand brain: values and story

steps.name: Define who counts as 'us' precisely
steps.does: Write the specific, checkable criteria for belonging to the cohort (a purchase count, a referral made, a value shared publicly), not a vague 'our best customers.'
steps.check: criteria are checkable against real data, not self-declared

steps.name: Identify who already advocates
steps.does: Pull customers who already advocate unprompted (unsolicited reviews, repeat referrals, organic social mentions) as the seed group.
steps.check: list is built from real behavior, not assumed loyalty

steps.name: Design what the group controls
steps.does: Design one real thing the cohort controls or gets first (early access, a say in a product decision, a named recognition), sized to what the brand can actually deliver.
steps.check: privilege is something the brand can sustain past the launch month

steps.name: Draft the invitation and rules
steps.does: Draft how members are invited, what is expected of them, and how membership could be lost.
steps.check: rules for losing membership are as clear as rules for gaining it

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the cohort design for founder approval before any invitation goes out.
steps.check: card states the ongoing cost of running this cohort, not just the launch cost

steps.name: Route execution
steps.does: Hand approved invitation copy to the email/SMS platform for the founder or Lifecycle specialist to send.
steps.check: this agent drafts only; it does not send

steps.name: Log for scale-up tracking
steps.does: Log the cohort design to the registry so a proven cohort can be handed to the Lifecycle specialist to run at scale.
steps.check: handoff point to Lifecycle is named explicitly

qa: membership criteria checkable, not self-declared
losing-membership rules as clear as gaining them
read_point: not a metric read; reviewed once the cohort is live for whether the design is sustainable.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours; founder review 2-4 days.

name: Operate the ambassador and community advocacy program
trigger: scheduled weekly, once a program is approved
human_role: what a community manager does every week to run an approved ambassador program
inputs_required: approved ambassador program design (from BRAND-W19 or an earlier program)
applicant list
brand guidelines and voice sheet

steps.name: Screen new applicants
steps.does: Check new applicants against the program's membership criteria.
steps.check: screening applies the same criteria to every applicant, no exceptions without a founder note

steps.name: Run a reputation check on new ambassadors
steps.does: Run a public reputation and controversy check on any new ambassador before onboarding.
steps.check: a flagged applicant is routed to founder review before onboarding

steps.name: Assign tasks
steps.does: Assign this week's content or advocacy tasks to active ambassadors, matched to what each one does well.
steps.check: no ambassador is assigned a task requiring a claim outside the approved tiers

steps.name: Check submitted content against guidelines
steps.does: Review submitted content against the brand guidelines and voice sheet before it is approved for reward or reposting.
steps.check: rejected content gets a specific, usable reason

steps.name: Track rewards owed
steps.does: Track what each ambassador is owed (discount, product, payment) against what they delivered.
steps.check: ledger computed in code, checked against the program's budget cap

steps.name: Flag budget or capacity issues
steps.does: Flag if the program is approaching its budget cap or if the team cannot keep up with volume.
steps.check: flag raised before the cap is hit, not after
steps.ask_founder_if: the program is within 10% of its budget cap

steps.name: Weekly log
steps.does: Log the week's activity, approvals, rejections and rewards to the registry.
steps.check: log is retrievable week over week for a program health trend

qa: screening criteria applied consistently
rewards computed in code against a real budget cap
reputation check run on every new ambassador
read_point: weekly operational log; program health reviewed monthly against BRAND-W19's original design.
typical_duration: agent time 2-4 hours per week.

name: Develop a PR angle, build the media list and source earned media
trigger: event: a launch or newsworthy moment | monthly sweep for thought-leadership and awards
human_role: what a PR manager does from a brand fact to a pitched, placed story
inputs_required: brand story and positioning
a specific launch, newsworthy moment, or founder expertise area
target media tier (trade press, mainstream, niche community)

steps.name: Find the pitchable angle
steps.does: Turn the brand story, a category frustration, or an origin fact into a pitchable press angle, not a product announcement.
steps.check: angle is newsworthy to a journalist, not just interesting to the founder

steps.name: Decide the earned-media lane
steps.does: Decide whether this moment fits a press pitch, a founder thought-leadership placement, or an awards/best-of submission, since each needs a different list and pitch.
steps.check: lane decision states why the other two lanes do not fit better this time

steps.name: Build the media list (press lane)
steps.does: Search for journalists and outlets whose beat matches this specific angle, verified as currently active on that beat.
steps.check: every contact's beat match is checked against their recent bylines, not an old media database entry

steps.name: Source thought-leadership slots (if that lane)
steps.does: Find podcasts, panels, and bylined-article slots that fit the founder's actual expertise and the brand's story.
steps.check: every opportunity matches a real, demonstrable area of founder expertise

steps.name: Track award and best-of calls (if that lane)
steps.does: Track industry awards and best-of list calls the brand qualifies for.
steps.check: only calls the brand actually qualifies for are shortlisted

steps.name: Seed through a few respected insiders, if applicable
steps.does: For a launch, consider seeding through a few respected insiders in a high-trust community before a broad press push.
steps.check: insiders are chosen for real relevance to the avatar's community, not just follower count

steps.name: Draft the pitch or submission
steps.does: Draft the pitch email, thought-leadership pitch, or award submission copy, claim-checked and in brand voice.
steps.check: every claim in the draft passes claim-check

steps.name: Founder or human sends
steps.does: This is human_assist: the founder or a person sends the actual pitch. The agent prepares everything up to the send.
steps.check: packet is ready to send with no missing field

steps.name: Log outcomes
steps.does: Log which pitches placed, which did not, and why, so future angles improve.
steps.check: a non-placement is logged with the reason given, not left blank

qa: media list beat-matched and freshly verified
every claim in a pitch passes claim-check
non-placements logged with reasons
read_point: tracked per pitch: placed, declined, or no response, reviewed monthly.
typical_duration: agent time 3-6 hours per angle; media outreach and response time adds 1-4 weeks.

name: Monitor reputation risk and draft a crisis holding statement
trigger: alert-driven: a spike in complaints, viral criticism, or a factual attack is detected | on demand
human_role: what a PR manager does the moment something starts going wrong publicly
inputs_required: public mention and review monitoring signal
brand facts to verify or refute a claim
founder availability for rapid review

steps.name: Detect the spike
steps.does: Watch public mentions and reviews for a sudden spike in complaint volume, a viral criticism, or a specific factual attack.
steps.check: spike is measured against a baseline, not a single loud post

steps.name: Verify the underlying claim
steps.does: Check whether the criticism is factually accurate against the brand's own records before drafting any response.
steps.check: note states true, false, or partially true, with the evidence

steps.name: Assess severity and reach
steps.does: Estimate how far the criticism has spread and how much brand or revenue risk it carries.
steps.check: severity uses actual reach numbers where available, not a gut call

steps.name: Draft a holding statement
steps.does: Draft a short holding statement acknowledging the issue and stating what happens next, without over-promising or admitting an unverified fault.
steps.check: statement makes no claim the fact verification note does not support

steps.name: Draft the escalation note
steps.does: Write who inside the brand needs to see this now and what decision they need to make.
steps.check: escalation note names a specific person and a specific decision, not 'someone should look at this'

steps.name: Founder gate before anything is posted
steps.does: This is always founder_gate: nothing is posted, replied to, or sent publicly without founder review.
steps.check: no public response goes out without this step

steps.name: Log and monitor after response
steps.does: Log what was said and continue monitoring for 48-72 hours to see if the issue is resolving.
steps.check: monitoring continues past the first response, not a one-time check

qa: nothing posted without founder review
statement makes no unverified claim
monitoring continues after the response
read_point: immediate at detection; re-checked at 48-72 hours after response.
typical_duration: agent time 1-3 hours to prepare; founder decision needed within hours for a live crisis.

name: Run the partnership pipeline: source, screen and clear
trigger: twice yearly sourcing sweep | on demand when a specific collaboration is proposed
human_role: what a partnerships lead does from a cold sourcing sweep to a cleared, briefed collaboration
inputs_required: avatar record (who the partner should also serve)
current category and non-competitive adjacent categories
a specific proposal, if screening one rather than sourcing

steps.name: Source candidates (sweep)
steps.does: Proactively search for non-competitive brands serving the same avatar, twice a year, before any specific proposal exists.
steps.check: every candidate serves the same avatar without competing in the same category

steps.name: Screen for category overlap
steps.does: Check a candidate or a proposed partner for direct category overlap; default to non-competitive brands.
steps.check: overlap verdict is explicit: none, adjacent, or competing

steps.name: Screen for narrative fit
steps.does: Check whether the collaboration tells a story either brand's customer would actually want, not just a co-marketing convenience.
steps.check: verdict names the specific shared story, not 'it could work'

steps.name: Run the reputation check
steps.does: Run a public reputation and controversy check on the other party before any agreement moves forward.
steps.check: a flag here stops the process until the founder reviews it

steps.name: Draft the brief, if screened favorably
steps.does: Draft what the collaboration would look like: format, duration, what each side contributes, and rough terms.
steps.check: brief states the specific customer value, not just brand exposure

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the screened candidate and brief for founder approval before any outreach is made.
steps.check: card shows all 3 screen results (overlap, narrative fit, reputation) together

steps.name: Re-check yearly for ongoing relationships
steps.does: For an approved, ongoing partnership, re-run the reputation check yearly.
steps.check: re-check happens on schedule, not only when a problem is already visible

steps.name: Log the pipeline
steps.does: Log sourced candidates, screening outcomes and founder decisions to the registry.
steps.check: a rejected candidate's reason is kept so the same pitch is not repeated unchanged

reputation check always run before agreement
annual re-check on ongoing partnerships
read_point: sourcing sweep twice yearly; screening as proposals arrive; reputation re-check yearly on live partnerships.
typical_duration: agent time 2-4 hours per candidate; founder review 2-5 days.

name: Design an event or pop-up
trigger: on demand
human_role: what an events lead designs when the exact target customer already gathers somewhere real
inputs_required: avatar record: where this customer actually gathers in person
team capacity (who can staff it)
budget ledger

steps.name: Name where the avatar already gathers
steps.does: Identify a real place or occasion the target avatar already gathers (a wedding expo, a college fest, a farmers' market, a festival pop-up), not a generic venue.
steps.check: each candidate names a real, checkable gathering, not an assumed one

steps.name: Size to team capacity
steps.does: Size the activation to what the team can actually run by hand, not a scaled-up fantasy version.
steps.check: concept states exactly how many people are needed to staff it

steps.name: Design the guerrilla or pop-up format
steps.does: Design the specific format: a sampling booth, a pop-up shop-in-shop, a small guerrilla activation, matched to the occasion.
steps.check: format matches the venue's real constraints (footfall, permission needed, timing)

steps.name: Budget the activation
steps.does: Cost the activation (space, staff, materials, any permit or vendor fee) against the ledger.
steps.check: budget checked against the ledger before proceeding
steps.ask_founder_if: the budget would exceed the working stop

steps.name: Plan the read
steps.does: Define what success looks like and how it will be measured (footfall, samples given, codes redeemed, follow-on online sales in the following days).
steps.check: read plan has a specific metric and a specific measurement date

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the full plan and budget for founder approval before any booking or spend commitment.
steps.check: card shows budget and read plan together

steps.name: Log and route execution

steps.check: handoff packet has every logistics detail the plan specified

qa: venue is real and checkable
budget checked against the ledger before commitment
read plan has a specific metric and date

name: Run competitive intelligence: win-loss and battlecards
trigger: quarterly win-loss research | on demand battlecard build, or when a named competitor materially changes
human_role: what a competitive-intelligence lead does to arm support and the founder with real comparison language
inputs_required: named competitor
recent near-miss and win customers, if running win-loss
competitor packet (BRAND-W04)

steps.name: Sample near-miss and win customers

steps.check: sample includes both directions (near-miss and win), not just one

steps.name: Ask why, in their own words

steps.check: questions are open, matching the interview-guide standard

steps.name: Verify the differences named

steps.check: every difference is checked against a current, dated source

steps.name: Build the battlecard

qa: differences verified against current, dated sources
battlecard stays internal unless separately cleared
win-loss questions open, not leading
read_point: quarterly for win-loss; on demand for battlecard refresh.
typical_duration: agent time 3-5 hours; win-loss interviews add 1-2 weeks for scheduling.

name: Run a wild bet from idea to stage gate to execution brief
trigger: monthly backlog sourcing | event: a specific wild bet is proposed or approved
human_role: what a new-ventures lead does from a raw idea to a bounded, briefed bet the team can actually run
inputs_required: contribution margin and team capacity from the metric contract
brand brain: values and category norms
the wild bet's type: new line, new market, licensing, wholesale, or retail pop-up

steps.name: Source and log backlog ideas
steps.does: Continuously source wild bet candidates from adjacent industries, category norms worth breaking, and gaps the brand's own research has surfaced. Keep a dated backlog.
steps.check: every entry names the category norm it would break or the gap it fills

steps.name: Screen a proposed bet against the backlog and brand fit
steps.does: When a bet is proposed (by the founder, or pulled from the backlog), check it against brand values and current capacity before bounding it.
steps.check: a bet that conflicts with a stated brand value is flagged, not silently bounded anyway

steps.name: Decide the bet type
steps.does: Classify the bet as a new product line, a new market, a licensing deal, a wholesale/retail entry, or a retail pop-up, since each routes to a different feasibility check.
steps.check: classification determines exactly one routing path below

steps.name: Run the type-specific feasibility pass
steps.does: New line: size against BRAND-W11 market sizing. New market: check regulatory, tax, competitor and logistics feasibility for the target country or region. Licensing: check royalty norms, score the licensee, draft deal-memo terms. Wholesale/retail: build the line sheet and buyer pitch kit, and check channel/packaging fit against DTC, marketplace and retail formats.
steps.output: feasibility packet, shaped to the bet type
steps.check: packet names the specific constraint each type check found, not a generic 'looks feasible'

steps.name: Write the 8-field bound
steps.does: Write the hypothesis, category norm broken, budget cap, downside cap (as a share of contribution margin, computed in code), cohort and size, control design, stop rule, read-point date, and legal/consent flag.
steps.check: all 8 fields present and specific; downside cap computed in code, not estimated

steps.name: Flag legal review if warranted
steps.does: Flag for legal review if the bet promises something, mails or texts people, or gates access in a way that carries legal exposure.
steps.check: flag defaults to 'needs review' when uncertain, never defaults to 'clear'

steps.name: Founder gate on the bound
steps.does: Present the bound for founder approval before anything launches. No wild bet runs on the bound alone without this step.
steps.check: a bound with no read point or stop rule is never presented as ready

steps.name: Write the type-specific execution brief
steps.does: Turn the approved bound into an execution brief sized to the smallest group the team can serve by hand, sequenced through the checks the bet's type requires (for example: retail pop-up sequences packaging and channel fit before a buyer pitch; licensing sequences the deal memo before any product ships).
steps.check: brief names every check completed before launch, in order

steps.name: Founder gate on the brief
steps.does: Present the execution brief for a final founder go/no-go before work starts.
steps.check: go/no-go is explicit, not implied by silence

steps.name: Log and set the read reminder
steps.does: Log the bound and brief to the registry, and set a reminder for the stated read-point date so the bet is judged on schedule, not forgotten.
steps.output: registry entry with a scheduled read-point check
steps.check: read point is a specific date, not 'later'

qa: downside cap computed in code as a share of contribution margin
all 8 bound fields present and specific
legal-review flag defaults to caution
read-point date is scheduled, not left open-ended
read_point: set explicitly in the bound at approval time; this workflow does not itself score the outcome, it schedules that check.
typical_duration: agent time 1-3 days depending on bet type; founder review 3-7 days across the two gates; a new-market feasibility pass can add 1-2 weeks.

name: Run an AI-persona pretest before a real research round
trigger: on demand, before spending on a real survey, interview round, or paid message test
human_role: what a researcher does to catch an obvious miss cheaply before paying for a real round
inputs_required: messaging, naming or concept shortlist to pretest
avatar record to build the persona from
budget ledger

steps.name: Check the budget
steps.does: Confirm the ledger has room before running any paid AI-persona pass.
steps.check: checked before the call, not after
steps.ask_founder_if: this would exceed the working stop

steps.name: Build the persona from real evidence
steps.does: Build the simulated persona strictly from the existing avatar record's job, forces and quotes, not from a generic stereotype.
steps.check: every trait in the persona brief traces to the avatar record

steps.name: Run the pass on the shortlist
steps.does: Run the simulated persona against the messaging, naming or concept shortlist and record its reactions.
steps.check: notes are labeled 'simulated, not a real customer' everywhere they are shown

steps.name: Flag obvious misses only
steps.does: Use the pass only to catch obvious misses (confusing wording, an unintended reading, a flat concept), never to declare a winner.
steps.check: output never ranks candidates as if this were real customer data

steps.name: Decide whether a real round is still needed
steps.does: State plainly that this pretest does not replace the planned real survey or interview round; it only trims the shortlist first.
steps.check: trimmed shortlist still goes to the real research round, not treated as final

steps.name: Log the pretest
steps.does: Log the pretest and its cost to the registry and budget ledger.
steps.check: cost logged against the ledger, not left untracked

qa: persona built from real avatar evidence, not stereotype
output never presented as if it were real customer data
budget checked before the call
read_point: not a metric read; this is a cheap filter before the real read comes from the survey, interview or test that follows.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 hours.

name: Advise the founder on brand-building operating practices
trigger: on demand
human_role: what an operating advisor does to turn recurring patterns into short, reusable guidance
inputs_required: registry history of past brand decisions and their outcomes
founder's stated operating question (hiring sequence, ideation method, decision speed, readiness checks)

steps.name: Name the operating question
steps.does: State the specific recurring pattern the founder is asking about (when to hire for a brand role, how fast to decide on a name, when a brand is ready for a wild bet).
steps.check: question is specific enough to answer with a checklist, not a philosophy

steps.name: Pull the registry history
steps.does: Pull past decisions and outcomes on this pattern from the registry (past naming timelines, past wild bet readiness, past hire timing).
steps.check: history pull uses this brand's real past decisions, not general theory alone

steps.name: Draw the pattern
steps.does: State what actually correlated with a good outcome versus a bad one in this brand's own history.
steps.check: pattern is stated with the evidence count behind it (how many past cases)

steps.name: Write short, reusable guidance
steps.does: Turn the pattern into a short checklist or rule of thumb the founder can reuse without re-deriving it each time.
steps.check: guidance fits on one page and gives a clear yes/no test

steps.name: Founder review
steps.does: Present the guidance for the founder to confirm it matches their own read of what has worked.
steps.check: founder can accept, edit or reject the guidance

steps.name: Log for reuse
steps.does: File the accepted guidance where future runs of this agent (or the founder) can find it again.
steps.check: guidance is retrievable by the operating question it answers

qa: pattern grounded in this brand's real history, not generic advice
guidance gives a clear yes/no test
read_point: not a metric read; revisited if a later decision contradicts the guidance.
typical_duration: agent time 1-2 hours.

name: Brief packaging artwork and mandatory label placement
trigger: event: new SKU, new channel, or a packaging change
human_role: what a packaging coordinator briefs before artwork goes to print
inputs_required: product spec from the Product and Supply specialist (PROD-C13)
target channel(s): DTC, marketplace, retail
brand guidelines (visual language section)

steps.name: Pull the product spec
steps.does: Pull the dieline, net quantity, and any per-channel packaging constraint from the Product and Supply specialist's spec.
steps.check: spec is pulled, never re-derived from guesswork

steps.name: Apply the visual language
steps.does: Apply the brand guidelines' palette, typography and logo rules to the dieline layout.
steps.check: layout follows the logo clear-space and minimum-size rules

steps.name: Place mandatory declarations
steps.does: Place every legally required declaration for the target market. US: net quantity and manufacturer/packer/distributor name and address (FTC Fair Packaging and Labeling Act), Care Labeling Rule for textiles, Prop 65 warning where required, and FTC Jewelry Guides quality marks where the product is jewelry. India (markets: IN, null for US): MRP, Legal Metrology details (net quantity, manufacturer/packer/importer name and address, month and year of manufacture, consumer care contact), BIS or hallmark mark where the product category requires it, and the EPR mark where applicable.
steps.check: every mandatory field for this product category is present and legible at the required minimum size

steps.name: Check channel-specific rules
steps.does: Check any marketplace-specific packaging or labeling rule (for example, marketplace return-label or barcode placement requirements) beyond the general legal requirements.
steps.check: each target channel's specific rule is checked, not assumed same as DTC

steps.name: Run the completeness check
steps.does: Run the full checklist of mandatory declarations against the layout before it is called ready.
steps.check: a missing mandatory field blocks sign-off, it does not go to print with a note to 'fix later'

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the brief and checklist result for founder sign-off before it goes to a designer or printer.
steps.check: card shows the checklist result plainly

steps.name: Hand off and log
steps.does: Hand the approved brief to the designer or print vendor; log the version to the registry.
steps.check: version is tracked so a later channel addition updates from the current approved version, not an old one

qa: every mandatory declaration present and legible
channel-specific rules checked, not assumed
missing field blocks sign-off
read_point: not a metric read; a one-time brief per SKU/channel/packaging change, re-checked if the law or channel changes.
typical_duration: agent time 2-4 hours; founder review 1-2 days; print lead time is separate.

name: Manage a rebrand or repositioning program
trigger: on demand, when a rebrand or repositioning is warranted
human_role: what a brand lead runs when the identity itself, not just a campaign, needs to change
inputs_required: evidence the current brand is failing to win (from BRAND-W17 perception-gap audit, BRAND-W18 brand health, or a founder call)
current brand guidelines, positioning, and catalogue

steps.name: Audit brand equity
steps.does: Assess what the current brand actually owns in the customer's mind (from BRAND-W17's perception-gap findings and BRAND-W18's health trend), separate from what the founder wishes it owned.
steps.check: audit is grounded in the last 2 quarters of real findings, not a fresh guess

steps.name: Decide what to keep
steps.does: Name what survives the rebrand (an equity asset, a color, a customer relationship) versus what changes.
steps.check: every 'keep' item names the equity reason it survives

steps.name: Expect and plan catalogue pruning
steps.does: Flag that a rebrand usually forces catalogue pruning (SKUs that only made sense under the old story) and name likely candidates.
steps.check: a pruning candidate names the specific story mismatch, not just low sales

steps.name: Sequence the program
steps.does: Sequence the actual work: positioning (BRAND-W10), naming if needed (BRAND-W12), voice and story (BRAND-W14), visual identity and guidelines (BRAND-W16), then a phased rollout across site, ads and packaging.
steps.check: plan sequences dependencies correctly (positioning before voice, voice before guidelines)

steps.name: Set the real trigger metric
steps.does: Set the metric the rebrand is meant to move (brand health trend, repeat rate, or a stated perception-gap closing), not vanity attention.
steps.check: metric already exists in the metric contract; nothing invented for this program

steps.name: Founder gate
steps.does: Present the full program, sequencing and trigger metric for founder approval before any phase starts, since this touches every other brand workflow.
steps.check: founder approves the sequence, not just the idea of rebranding

steps.name: Run the sequenced phases
steps.does: Execute each phase workflow in order, routing to BRAND-W10, W12, W14 and W16 as sequenced, each with its own founder gate.
steps.check: no phase starts before its dependency phase is founder-approved

steps.name: Measure by shipped artifacts against the real trigger
steps.does: Measure the program's success by what actually shipped and moved the trigger metric, against a real prior trend, not a launch-week spike.
steps.check: readout compares to the pre-rebrand trend, not just a single before/after point

steps.name: Log the program
steps.does: Log the full program, decisions and readout to the registry.
steps.check: readout is honest about what did not move, not only what did

qa: equity audit grounded in real recent findings
dependencies sequenced correctly
readout compared to a real prior trend, not a spike
read_point: set at program approval, measured against the pre-rebrand trend after the full sequence ships.
typical_duration: agent time spans the full program (weeks to months); each phase carries its own workflow's duration.
